hypothesis: A smooth rank-distance target will give focused attack/concession CEM enough effective discovery samples while retaining rare-tail targeting
design: One scout-selected tail, three pure-Q discovery batches of up to 800 samples, independent validation, frozen fresh production. The smooth discovery score weighted nearby ranks around the rare frontier; no reference probabilities entered the estimator.
reason: The broad kernel moved the fit toward P and reduced targeted production. The narrow kernel restored targeting but added no ESS>=10 cells and reduced ESS>=25 coverage. Both remained behind equal-work plain MC; the prior adjacent-window CEM trial also failed at 20 seeds. Further tuning of this proposal family is not warranted.
